text.title: max-turns-circuit-breaker Core Rules
text.summary: Migrated testable rules for max-turns-circuit-breaker. Verify and refine before relying on for production.

rule.statement: Set max_turns explicitly on every production agent invocation (5-10 retrieval, 15-20 coding) and wrap the call in a try/except that handles MaxTurnsExceeded by summarizing the partial trajectory with a cheap model and returning a graceful reply.
rule.rationale: Tool loops fail by silent budget burn — the LLM treats each tool result as progress regardless of whether the goal is closer. A hard cap is the only deterministic stop. Catching the exception (instead of letting it bubble) preserves the partial trace and turns a 500 into a usable answer.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, agent_kind is high-tier (coding or planning — the kinds whose r1 ranges sit above retrieval's 5-10) and per_turn_cost_usd is advanced (at or above $0.10 per turn, the fm-01 setting where 50 turns bill $5), the circuit-breaker-spec MUST set max_turns at the bottom of the kind's range — 15 for coding, 10 for planning — and never above 20 (fm-04's CI lint), MUST record worst-case cost per run as max_turns × per_turn_cost_usd and show it is inside the caller's per-run budget, MUST set recovery_model to a haiku-class model with recovery capped at one LLM call and at most $0.01 per recovery (fm-03), MUST set log_partial_trajectory to true, and MUST give fallback_message_template the turns consumed and the summarised partial trajectory. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (max_turns, MaxTurnsExceeded); LangGraph documentation (recursion_limit, GraphRecursionError); failure modes fm-01, fm-03 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: At a dime a turn the cap is the bill: the difference between 15 and 20 turns on a coding agent is fifty cents per failure, multiplied by every silent loop. Pinning the cap at the range floor and writing the worst-case cost into the spec is what makes the budget reviewable before the first loop, and the haiku-class recovery keeps the failure path from costing more than the run it rescued.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, agent_kind is high-tier (coding or planning) and per_turn_cost_usd is not advanced (under $0.10 per turn, the fm-01 line), the circuit-breaker-spec MUST set max_turns inside the kind's range — 15-20 for coding, 10-15 for planning — with a CI lint rejecting any value above 20 (fm-04), MUST wrap the run in a catch for the framework's turn-limit exception (MaxTurnsExceeded in the OpenAI Agents SDK, GraphRecursionError in LangGraph) that returns a rendered fallback_message_template instead of a 500 (fm-02), MUST set recovery_model to a haiku-class model with recovery capped at one LLM call (fm-03), and MUST set log_partial_trajectory to true so the partial trace reaches the log before the fallback is returned. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (max_turns, MaxTurnsExceeded); LangGraph documentation (recursion_limit); failure modes fm-02, fm-03 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Coding and planning agents legitimately need more turns than retrieval, so the range is wider, but a cap above 20 turns a failure into a 90-second wait before the user learns anything (fm-04). The catch is what converts the framework's exception from a 500 into an answer, and the logged partial trajectory is the only evidence left of why the loop did not converge.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and agent_kind is low-tier (retrieval, the r1 kind with the 5-10 range), the circuit-breaker-spec MUST set max_turns between 5 and 10, MUST catch the framework's turn-limit exception and return fallback_message_template rather than re-raising (fm-02), and MUST set recovery_model to a haiku-class model or to none — a static fallback message with zero LLM calls is acceptable on this tier because a retrieval trajectory of at most 10 turns needs no summarisation — and MAY set log_partial_trajectory to false when the tool results are already logged by the retrieval layer. Raising max_turns above 10 on this tier requires a rejected-alternatives entry naming the driver that forced it. audit.rule_refs cites r1.

rationale.source: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (max_turns); failure modes fm-02 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A retrieval agent that has not found its answer in ten turns is not going to find it in fifty; fm-04's 90-second failure is exactly a retrieval agent with a coding cap. Because the trajectory is short and the per-turn cost low, the expensive part of the recovery story can be dropped without losing the guarantee that matters, which is that the run stops and the user sees a message.
